master.headline: The infrastructure around the model.
master.lead: Perseus Computing builds a three-product platform for AI workflows inside the operating boundary: Context Engine resolves live, bounded context; Perseus Vault retains governed local memory; Ledger records evidence, authority, and time. The platform is designed for on-premises, disconnected, and controlled-network deployments.
master.problem: AI can produce a plausible answer while losing the state that made it useful. The next operator then has to reconstruct the repository state, prior decision, or evidence trail before work can continue.
master.change: Perseus joins context before action, governed memory across sessions, and evidence after action at the workflow boundary—without claiming to replace the model, mission platform, prime integrator, or approving authority.
master.discussion: Bring one bounded workflow, its data boundary, and the integration surface that needs to be made reviewable; the Hanscom small-business relationship can help identify the right technical owner or partner route.
master.engagement: Route snapshot: NV074 primary; NV027/CPSP exploratory; Tradewinds optional. DICE submitted; two Phase I + two D2P2 SBIR proposals submitted in the prior round; AFRL/ISW whitepaper in SME review since 21 July. Status only—no awards or endorsements claimed.
fit_rows: Software factories, resilient C2, and distributed decision workflows where a local context/memory/evidence layer can support a qualified mission team.
AI/ML, DevSecOps, RMF evidence, cyber, and enterprise IT workflows where state and provenance must stay inside the controlled network.
Partner-led support where local, reviewable AI connects to sensing, EW, PNT, or mission-system workflows.

cyber-networks.headline: Controlled AI workflows need state and evidence that survive the handoff.
cyber-networks.lead: Perseus combines Context Engine, Perseus Vault, and Ledger to keep working context, governed memory, and evidence lineage inside the controlled environment where an AI/ML or DevSecOps workflow runs.
cyber-networks.problem: AI-assisted cyber and DevSecOps workflows often lose the state that made an answer useful: the current repository, ticket, deployment, source commitment, or prior decision. That gap makes review, handoff, and risk acceptance harder.
cyber-networks.change: Context Engine resolves bounded workflow state before action; Vault preserves local, time-aware memory; Ledger can package captured inputs, approvals, actions, and served context for downstream review. Perseus is an evidence layer—not an automated cATO platform.
cyber-networks.discussion: Use the C&N Industry Meeting Request Form for a short conversation about one bounded AI/ML, DevSecOps, or RMF evidence workflow, its data boundary, and the integration surface between the agent and existing tools.
cyber-networks.engagement: C&N intake is through the current Microsoft Forms industry-meeting page. Use unclassified, non-sensitive details; no C&N meeting, cATO authorization, or Government endorsement is claimed.
fit_rows: Evidence-aware context and governed memory for controlled model-assisted workflows.
Ledger provenance and bounded context envelopes that can sit beside control, POA&M, monitoring, and engineering systems.
Local deployment where cloud memory, external telemetry, or opaque state is out of bounds.

c3bm.headline: Make AI-enabled C2 and software delivery reviewable across the handoff.
c3bm.lead: Perseus gives AI-enabled C2 and software-factory workflows a local Context Engine, governed Vault memory, and Ledger evidence layer—an enabling component that can sit beside the mission platform.
c3bm.problem: Distributed teams and agents move through repositories, decisions, operational artifacts, and evolving mission context. When state disappears between sessions or handoffs, software-factory work becomes harder to review, re-plan, and trust.
c3bm.change: Context Engine supplies a bounded starting state, Vault preserves the working record across sessions, and Ledger records what was used and what happened. The contribution is intentionally modular so a prime or mission-system owner can retain system authority.
c3bm.discussion: Bring one software-factory, resilient-C2, or distributed-decision workflow, the handoffs that fail today, and the existing integration surface; we are seeking the right technical owner or SBO carve-out route, not claiming an existing C3BM integration.
c3bm.engagement: C3BM is a warm Hanscom small-business route after the 14 August meeting. The objective is technical routing for a bounded enabling component; prior proposals are R&D status facts, not C3BM sponsorship or awards.
fit_rows: Durable context across agent sessions, repositories, tickets, deployments, and engineering handoffs.
Evidence-backed memory for workflows that must be re-planned, handed off, and reviewed.
A modular contribution that can support a prime-led system and possible small-business carve-out without replacing the mission platform.

electronic-systems.headline: A local evidence layer around mission-system AI.
electronic-systems.lead: Perseus provides Context Engine, Perseus Vault, and Ledger around an AI-enabled mission workflow; sensing, EW, PNT, embedded inference, and prime-system integration remain partner-led responsibilities.
electronic-systems.problem: Mission-system teams need to know what data an AI assistant saw, what it retained, how current it was, and how a decision can be reviewed without moving the working record outside the program boundary.
electronic-systems.change: Context Engine renders bounded mission context, Vault retains local and time-aware memory, and Ledger records evidence and authority boundaries. The three products form an inspectable support layer while the mission owner retains hardware, safety, and authorization responsibility.
electronic-systems.discussion: Bring a specific sensing, EW, PNT, or mission-system integration boundary, its deployment constraints, and the prime or technical partner role that Perseus could support.
electronic-systems.engagement: An AFRL/ISW whitepaper has been in front of an ISW Division SME since 21 July. This brief is a broader routing/partner conversation—not a duplicate follow-up or sponsorship claim.
fit_rows: Context and evidence support where local AI must remain close to the mission workflow.
Governed memory, temporal state, and provenance without requiring a cloud memory service.
A bounded infrastructure contribution for a prime, integrator, or domain performer that owns mission hardware and test authority.
